prize_parts.citation: For the rational design of molecular-sieve catalysts with controlled pore architecture and active sites

statement.case_for: B003 is a case of structure determining function that changed an entire industry. Organic structure-directing agents, new framework topologies and tailored acid and metal sites let chemists design a pore and place an active site. The result is the catalytic backbone of refining, petrochemistry and emissions control, and it is now extending to biomass and Lewis-acid catalysis. Decades of independent confirmation and industrial deployment mean maturity is not a question. Corma (design and industrial transfer), Zones (structure-directing agents and the SSZ family) and Davis (new frameworks and Lewis-acid and hierarchical zeolites) form a defensible trio with clear and distinct contributions. As a structural chemist I also note that the claims in this field are checkable. The frameworks and the location of active sites were established by diffraction and microscopy, not inferred. That is the evidentiary standard I trust.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that this is a field-level achievement with a diffuse credit chain. Jihong Yu, Tsapatsis and many structure-solution and synthesis groups are left out, and a three-person cut may look arbitrary. Zeolite catalysis also has the weakest novelty narrative of my candidates for a lay audience, because it can read as incremental refinement of a mature technology. The committee will have to articulate what is conceptually new (rational design with organic templates) rather than rewarding industrial importance alone. Opening support is thin, with only one first-place vote, and I should not mistake my own field proximity for broad merit.

responses.point: Linke ranks base editing (B050) first as a clear chemical principle, deaminase chemistry in a defined editing window, with a general capability and clinical use, while noting its closeness to the 2020 CRISPR prize and the Kondo/Nishida attribution complication.
responses.response: I agree that the chemistry is neat and the impact is real. My reservation is the one Linke raises himself. A decade-old tool built on a Cas scaffold that the committee honoured in 2020 will be read as a sequel, and a prize naming two former trainees alongside Liu is an attribution choice we would have to defend. The molecular-level evidence also concerns editing outcomes rather than a new structural or mechanistic insight. I do not oppose B050 and keep it as a serious option, but I would not rank it above a mature, fully validated design principle with no overlap problem.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks targeted protein degradation (B042) first as a simple, conceptually clean chemical idea that opens the undruggable proteome, and stresses that attribution to Crews, Deshaies and Handa is the hard part.
responses.response: I agree B042 is one of the most consequential new modalities, and I name it as my first alternative. I part ways on maturity. No PROTAC is yet an approved drug, and the allocation among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli and others reflects two different strands, PROTACs and molecular glues, that may not belong to one citation. The ternary-complex structural basis is well documented, which I value, but the clinical validation Aqvist implicitly relies on is still pending. If degraders reach approval in the next few years, I would move it up.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks long-range protein electron transfer (B020, Gray and Winkler) first, as a quantitative physical mechanism established by time-resolved kinetics and overdue for recognition, and he treats serial femtosecond crystallography (B015) as a method that makes dynamics visible.
responses.response: On B015 I largely share his view. Serial crystallography at XFELs is a diffraction-before-destruction method that made microcrystal and time-resolved structures possible, and I name it as an alternative. His own caveat applies, though: the founding group is large (Chapman, Fromme, Schlichting, Spence, Hajdu) and the three-name limit is awkward. On B020, I accept the physical-mechanism case and the clean two-person credit, but the Ru-modified-protein experiments are elegant model-system work. I want to be convinced that the committee would be recognising a broadly enabling concept, not a deep but narrower program. I am open to being persuaded.

responses.point: Chabes places base editing first and ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B052) third, arguing that both turn biology into defined chemical reactions or solutions and that LNP impact is overwhelming even though credit is spread across academia and industry.
responses.response: I take the LNP case seriously on impact, but the attribution issue is greater than Chabes allows. His own trio (Cullis, Hope, Madden) differs from Aili's and Sparr's trios, which swap in Anderson. That shows the credit split between Vancouver and Boston lineages, and between lipid design and process, is unresolved, and MacLachlan and Langer are also left out. The 2023 Medicine prize also covers part of the same translational story. I would want that resolved before I treat B052 as a leading candidate.

uncertainties: Whether a three-person cut of Corma, Davis and Zones will be accepted as fair given Yu, Tsapatsis and the structure-solution community.
Whether the committee will see rational molecular-sieve design as sufficiently novel in concept, not only important in industry.
Whether protein degradation will gain enough clinical validation, and a clean credit split between PROTACs and glues, to overtake mature design-principle candidates.
Whether base editing is judged independent enough from the 2020 CRISPR prize.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the preferred B003 candidates. I note proximity: my own research applies electron diffraction to zeolites, so I am in the same community as the B003 candidates and have probably cited or interacted with them. I have no documented collaboration, but the committee may wish to weigh this. My Stockholm University colleagueship with Secretary Brzezinski is not relevant to any shortlisted ballot.
